planner_json.title: Install, load and invoke Pi on both tracks through the pinned provider only
depends_on: GAW-1 (the adapter contract, declarations, stance table and real-cli test harness this adapter builds on)
GAW-2 (the stop_at option its must-ask entry passes to the runtime)

write_prohibited: .github/workflows/harness-eval.yml - Pi has no denied-write probe to wire
plugins/pixel-perfect/** - no plugin change in this task
Any file not listed in WRITE-ALLOWED

seed/pinned-pi.description: Pi at the pinned version installed by npm under a temp prefix with --ignore-scripts, a temp HOME, and an allowlisted env holding no provider key

specification.objective: Pi installs, loads and runs through the adapter contract on both tracks, and it can answer only through the pinned provider.
specification.success_state: A keyless load at 1.0.4 lists 11 of 11 skills from the plugin root with no model call. With no key, the real auth check prints `not_ready` and the check reads `pi-auth-not-ready` with 0 model requests. Each graded argv holds `--provider google` and `--model gemini-2.5-pro`. The registry serves this adapter.

requirements.description: GIVEN the pinned Pi CLI installed with `--ignore-scripts` in a temp HOME, with an allowlisted env holding no provider key WHEN the adapter's keyless load runs against this checkout, then its list THEN 11 of 11 command names appear, including `status` from `skill:pixel-perfect-status`, `observed_cli_version` reads `1.0.4` with `identity_decision.ok` true, and `model_request_count` stays 0
requirements.verification_service: real Pi CLI at the pinned version in a temp HOME
requirements.positive_example: Fresh temp HOME: identity approved at 1.0.4 and 11 names returned from get_commands with the plugin root as their source.
requirements.red: On base the registry answers pi-adapter-not-implemented, no load runs, and the command assertion fails.

scenario.verification_service: real Pi CLI at the pinned version in a temp HOME

would_fail_if: the list is a static array of names
a skill from outside the plugin root is counted
the --offline flag is omitted and a network call decides the list

build_proof.range: anything that proves Pi itself resolves the checkout's skills
examples: filtering get_commands by its own source path

steps: run the adapter's keyless load against this checkout, then its list

requirements.description: GIVEN that install with no provider key in the child env and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set to a placeholder in the parent env WHEN the preflight runs, and the graded entries' argv is read THEN the auth check prints `status` `not_ready`, the check reads `pi-auth-not-ready` with `model_request_count` 0, each argv holds `--provider` `google` and `--model` `gemini-2.5-pro`, and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is absent from the child env
requirements.verification_service: real Pi auth check and real JSON-mode run with no credential in the child env
requirements.positive_example: No key in the child env: auth check prints status not_ready, the adapter reads could-not-run pi-auth-not-ready, and no message_end from any provider exists.
requirements.red: On base no pi adapter exists, so the preflight reason is absent and this test fails.

scenario.verification_service: real Pi auth check and real JSON-mode run with no credential in the child env

would_fail_if: the preflight is removed and the run falls through to another provider's key
the argv uses the slash form, so the model id resolves on an alternate provider
the exit code is read as the verdict

build_proof.range: anything that proves Pi cannot answer through any provider but the pinned one
examples: --provider google in the argv and a provider check over the stream

steps: run the preflight with no provider key in the child env, and with OPENROUTER_API_KEY=placeholder in the parent env

must_not_observe: an argv holding the slash form `google/gemini-2.5-pro`
